sentences.text: In the aforesaid case, admittedly, the charge-sheet has not yet been filed and the investigation is still going on.
However, the parties have settled the matter out of the Court as, admittedly, FIR was lodged on 06.01.2024 in respect of the offence which committed from 30.11.2021 to 03.01.2024.

4. Counsel for the parties have submitted that the petitioner and the prosecturix were known to each other and only because of some misunderstanding the aforesaid FIR was lodged and subsequently they have settled the matter.

5. Both the parties were directed to appear before the Principal Registrar of this Court on 06.02.2024 and as per the report submitted by the OSD, parties have settled the matter on their own volition and the prosecutrix has also received a sum of Rs.15 lakhs, which according to her, she had given to the petitioner, which fact has also been accepted by the counsel for the petitioner.

6. Counsels have submitted that since the case is at its initial stage and even the charge-sheet has not been filed and it would not be anyone's benefit if the matter is tried before the trial Court, the outcome of which is a foregone conclusion.
7. Senior counsel for the respondent No.2 has submitted that an agreement has also been entered into between the parties, is also placed on record, which is signed by both the parties.
8. Counsel for the State has submitted that the appropriate orders may be passed.

9. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the considered opinion that since the prosecutrix has already settled the matter out of the Court with the petitioner and, admittedly, both of them are known to each other since long, this Court finds it expedient to allow the present petition.

Accordingly, the petition stands allowed and the FIR lodged at Crime No.6 of 2024 registered at Police Station Mahila Thana, Indore under Sections 376(2)(N), 377,
354(A), 384, 342, 328, 323 and 506 of IPC is hereby quashed.
Needless to say, the subsequent proceedings shall also stands quashed.
Since the petitioner is lodged in jail, it is directed that he shall be released forthwith.

(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE Pankaj Ronak Shukla vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10358938/
